# 1 Clement Chapter 47 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 47 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_047_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 47

**47:1** Take up the epistle of the blessed Paul the Apostle.

**47:2** What did he first write to you in the beginning of the gospel?

**47:3** In truth he wrote to you in the Spirit concerning himself and Cephas and Apollos, because even then you had made yourselves partisans.

**47:4** But that partisanship brought less sin upon you; for you were partisans of apostles attested by God, and of a man approved by them.

**47:5** But now consider who those are who have led you astray and who have diminished the honor of your celebrated brotherly love.

**47:6** It is shameful, beloved, exceedingly shameful and unworthy of your conduct in Christ, that on account of one or two persons the most steadfast and ancient church of the Corinthians is reported to be in revolt against the presbyters.

**47:7** And this report has reached not only us, but also those who differ from us — so that blasphemies are heaped upon the name of the Lord because of your folly, and danger is brought upon yourselves as well.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of Codex Alexandrinus with maximal literalness.*
